no: See Juan José Isach Mayo, `euclid 8164 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/8164>`__.
Contributed by Clark Kimberling and Peter Moses, March 26, 2025.

As a generalization of the triangles and circles introduced by Benjamin Warren, as in the preamble just before X_67624), let A' be the reflection of A in a point P = \(p : q : r\), let A'' be the reflection of A' in line BC, and define B'' and C'' cyclically. Then
Denote the triangle A"B"C" as WT(P) and its circumcircle as WC(P). The concentric circles WC(P) are listed here for selected points P. Specifically, the appearance of
means that the points X(i(1)), X(i(2)), ..., X(i(n)) lie on the circle XC(X(h)).

The points X_67714 - X_67892 are reflections in X_3 of points on the circles WC(X(k)). On such a circle, if {U, U'} and {V, V'} are pairs of antipodes, then UVU'V' is a rectangle inscribed in the circle. The appearance in the next list of
means that {X(i(k)), X(i(j))} is an antipodal pair of points on WC(X(h)).
